lines.name: Queen's Gambit Declined
lines.intro: Black declines the pawn with ...e6 and builds a solid wall on d5. You develop naturally, pin the f6 knight with Bg5, and put pressure on the c-file.

notes.0: Take the center and free the c1 bishop.
notes.1: Black stakes an equal claim to the center.
notes.2: The Queen's Gambit: offer a pawn to pull Black's d-pawn away from the center.
notes.3: Black declines and keeps d5 solid, though the c8 bishop is now shut in.
notes.6: Pin the knight against the queen. A pinned knight is a weaker defender of d5.
notes.8: Open the f1 bishop and support d4.
notes.10: Develop your last minor piece toward the center.
notes.11: Black develops and prepares ...c5 or ...e5 later.
notes.12: Put the rook on the c-file, where it will be strong once the file opens.
notes.13: Black reinforces d5 and makes room for the queen.
notes.14: Develop and get ready to castle. If ...dxc4, take back with the bishop.

lines.name: Queen's Gambit Accepted
lines.intro: Black takes the c4 pawn but can't hold it. You win it back with your bishop, get a free center, and develop quickly.

notes.0: Take the center and free the c1 bishop.
notes.1: Black stakes an equal claim to the center.
notes.2: The Queen's Gambit: offer a pawn to pull Black's d-pawn away from the center.
notes.4: Develop first. This stops ...e5, and the pawn on c4 isn't going anywhere.
notes.6: Open the bishop's path to c4.
notes.9: Black hits your center. This is the classic counter in the Queen's Gambit Accepted.
notes.11: Black prepares ...b5 to gain space and kick your bishop.
notes.12: Get the queen off the d-file and make room for a rook on d1.
notes.13: Black gains space and kicks the bishop.
notes.14: Drop back to b3, where the bishop still aims at e6 and f7.

lines.name: vs. Slav (2...c6)
lines.intro: In the Slav, Black defends d5 with ...c6 and keeps the c8 bishop free. Stop ...b5 with a4, then win the c4 pawn back and develop.

notes.0: Take the center and free the c1 bishop.
notes.1: Black stakes an equal claim to the center.
notes.2: The Queen's Gambit: offer a pawn to pull Black's d-pawn away from the center.
notes.3: The Slav: Black defends d5 with the c-pawn so the c8 bishop stays free.
notes.7: Black takes the pawn, hoping to hold it with ...b5.
notes.8: a4 stops ...b5, so Black can't keep the extra pawn.
notes.9: Black gets the bishop out before playing ...e6.
notes.10: Open the f1 bishop to win back c4.
notes.13: Black pins the c3 knight to make e4 harder to play.
notes.14: Castle. Next you aim for Qe2 and e4.
